- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before applying correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 75% of 30d mean, model is overconfident; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to catch early trend reversal.
